approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Junior Minerals Exploration Incentive) Bill 2017

The majority voted against an amendment to the usual second reading motion - which is a motion to read the bill for a second time, parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill. The amendment was introduced by Fenner MP [Andrew Leigh](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/fenner/andrew_leigh) (Labor). ### Motion text > *That all the words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House notes:* > > *(1) the Government failed to deliver an impact assessment of the previous Exploration Development Incentive; and* > > *(2) has failed to deliver for the people of Western Australia".*
Treasury Laws Amendment (Junior Minerals Exploration Incentive) Bill 2017 - in Committee - No exploration incentive for thermal coal

The bill replaces the former exploration development incentive with a $100 million junior minerals exploration incentive over four years from 2017-18, providing refundable tax offsets to investors in small exploration companies to address a 70% decline in greenfields exploration expenditure and the lack of a world-class mineral discovery in over 20 years.

The speaker argued that the Treasury Laws Amendment (Junior Minerals Exploration Incentive) Bill 2017 supports job growth, citing 400,000 new jobs in the past year (300,000 full-time) and record coal exports of $56.5 billion in 2017. They criticised Labor's anti-coal rhetoric and the National Australia Bank’s refusal to finance new thermal coal projects, urging support for the mining sector as essential for funding schools, hospitals and other services.
